title: Fresh Ginger Frozen Yoghurt
changes_from_base: Fresh and ground ginger are steeped in the warm gelatine whey before it is whisked back into the strained yoghurt.
summary: A zingy frozen yoghurt with the warmth of fresh and ground ginger. Smooth, creamy and full of spiced ginger character.
equipment: colander or sieve lined with three layers of muslin

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Drain the 900 g yoghurt in a colander lined with three layers of muslin, covered in the fridge for 8-12 h until 300 ml whey has drained.

steps.title: Whey
steps.text: Discard 180 ml whey from the drained liquid. Sprinkle 1 tsp gelatine over the remaining 120 ml whey, stand for 5 min, then microwave for about 30 s until bubbling at the edges and dissolved.

steps.title: Infuse
steps.text: Stir both 1 tbsp finely grated fresh ginger and 1 tsp ground ginger into the warm gelatine, cool for 5 min, then strain through a fine sieve, pressing the solids.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk 150 g caster sugar, 3 tbsp golden syrup, ⅛ tsp fine salt, the drained yoghurt and the ginger whey until the sugar dissolves.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Chill in the fridge or over an ice bath to 4 °C or below.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Churn in the ice-cream maker for 25-35 min to thick soft-serve, about -6 °C.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Freeze in an airtight container for at least 2 h; keeps for 5 days.

tips: Strain the ginger whey carefully through a fine sieve to remove solids and achieve a silky texture.
Chill the mixture thoroughly to 4 °C before churning for the best results.
Churn until thick soft-serve consistency, then freeze for a firmer scoop.
storage: Store in an airtight container in the freezer for up to 5 days.
